meta.title: Who really said "Family not only need to consist of merely those whom we share blood, but also for those whom we'd give blood"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Dickens never wrote it. The line is closing narration by Douglas McGrath for his 2002 Nicholas Nickleby film; the popular wording is a garbled retelling.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Family not only need to consist of merely those whom we share blood, but also for those whom we'd give blood'?
meta.ogDescription: Not Dickens. It's Vincent Crummles's closing narration in Douglas McGrath's 2002 film — no such line in the 1838–39 novel or in Mugby Junction.

answer.label: Not Charles Dickens — actually Douglas McGrath
answer.sourceLine: The sentence is closing narration written by Douglas McGrath for his 2002 film adaptation of Nicholas Nickleby, spoken by Vincent Crummles (Nathan Lane): “They came to see that family need not be defined merely as those with whom they share blood but for those for whom they would give their blood.” The version that circulates under Dickens’s name — ungrammatical, with its stray “not only… but also for” — is a later garbled retelling of that film line, and it appears nowhere in Dickens’s own 1838–39 novel ↗.

source.heading: Where the line actually comes from
source.excerpt: What happens when too early we lose a parent, that party on whom we rely for only everything? We must build a new family, person by person. … They came to see that family need not be defined merely as those with whom they share blood but for those for whom they would give their blood.
trail: Goodreads runs the popular wording under Dickens’s name with no book, chapter or date attached ↗ — 407 likes and not one citation. That absence is the first tell.

A cleaner variant, “Family need not be defined merely as those with whom we share blood, but as those for whom we would give our blood,” is filed on Goodreads under Nicholas Nickleby ↗. That is the film’s phrasing, credited to the novel — the classic signature of adaptation drift.

Film-quote databases put it where it belongs: Quotes.net transcribes it as Mr. Crummles in Nicholas Nickleby (2002) ↗, and Wikipedia ↗ confirms Douglas McGrath wrote and directed that film and that Nathan Lane both played Crummles and narrated.

We searched the Project Gutenberg texts directly: Nicholas Nickleby ↗, Mugby Junction ↗ and two dozen further Dickens volumes — about 26 MB of text — contain no instance of “share blood”, “give blood”, “give their blood” or “give our blood”.
source.excerptNote: Two passages from Crummles’s narration, separated in the film, as transcribed by Quotes.net ↗. Transcriptions of the second sentence vary slightly (“but for those for whom” / “but as those for whom”); we could not obtain the shooting script to settle it.

source.rightsHolder: Douglas McGrath and the rights holders in the 2002 Nicholas Nickleby screenplay
source.rightsNote: Everything Charles Dickens actually wrote is long in the public domain — he died in 1870, and Nicholas Nickleby is free at Project Gutenberg ↗. This sentence is not his. The oldest source we could document for it is a film released in December 2002 ↗, so the screenplay is squarely in copyright; the mangled wording that circulates under Dickens’s name is an anonymous derivative of that line with no identified author, and no public-domain status can be claimed for either.

author.name: Douglas McGrath
author.heading: Who actually wrote it
author.bio: Douglas McGrath was born in Midland, Texas on 12 February 1958 and began his writing career on Saturday Night Live. He co-wrote Bullets Over Broadway (1994) with Woody Allen, earning an Academy Award nomination, then wrote and directed Emma (1996) and Nicholas Nickleby (2002). He died in New York City on 3 November 2022, aged 64, of a heart attack while performing his solo show — and, in one of the odder legacies a screenwriter can have, at least two of his invented lines now circulate worldwide as Charles Dickens’s.

cite.sourceCitation: Douglas McGrath, writer and director, Nicholas Nickleby (2002), closing narration spoken by Vincent Crummles (Nathan Lane); line as transcribed at Quotes.net. No comparable sentence appears in Charles Dickens, The Life and Adventures of Nicholas Nickleby (1838–39), or in Mugby Junction (1866).

copyAttribution: Not Charles Dickens. The line is closing narration written by Douglas McGrath for his 2002 film "Nicholas Nickleby," spoken by Vincent Crummles: "They came to see that family need not be defined merely as those with whom they share blood but for those for whom they would give their blood." The popular wording — "Family not only need to consist of merely those whom we share blood, but also for those whom we'd give blood" — is a later garbled retelling, and appears in none of Dickens's works. — Quotle.info

misattribution.heading: The attribution, untangled
misattribution.intro: This is a three-stage misattribution: a screenwriter’s line, mangled by retelling, then retro-fitted to a Dickens book that has nothing to do with it.

items.why: Vincent Crummles’s closing narration, transcribed at Quotes.net ↗ as “They came to see that family need not be defined merely as those with whom they share blood but for those for whom they would give their blood.” Wikipedia ↗ credits McGrath as writer-director and Nathan Lane as both Crummles and the film’s narrator.

“Family not only need to consist of merely those whom we share blood, but also for those whom we’d give blood” is not a sentence Dickens or McGrath would have let stand. Goodreads carries it with no source whatsoever ↗, liked by over 400 readers. A tidier variant is filed there under Nicholas Nickleby ↗ — the film’s phrasing, credited to the novel.

items.scope: The book it gets pinned on
items.why: A print-on-demand publisher issued an edition whose title contains the quote ↗ (A Word To The Wise, 20 August 2013). Retail listings then read as sourcing. The actual text ↗ contains nothing like it.

items.who: Other “Dickens” lines from the same screenplay
items.why: “Happiness is a gift and the trick is not to expect it, but to delight in it when it comes” is also Crummles in the 2002 film, transcribed alongside the family line ↗. Lydia Craig’s research, summarised by Loyola University Chicago ↗, notes that misattributed Dickens quotes were “occasionally… derived from screenplays of Dickens films, such as Douglas McGrath’s Nicholas Nickleby.”

misattribution.truthLine: Dickens (7 February 1812 – 9 June 1870) wrote the novel; a screenwriter born 88 years after him wrote the sentence. Wikiquote’s Dickens page ↗ does not list the line in any section, sourced or misattributed.

context.heading: Why this one travelled
lead: The line does real work in the film. McGrath’s Nicholas Nickleby is bookended by Vincent Crummles talking straight to the audience, and the closing narration is the moral of the adaptation: Nicholas loses a father, and assembles a household out of Smike, the Cheerybles, Newman Noggs and the Crummles troupe. “We must build a new family, person by person,” Crummles says earlier in the same speech. It is a warm, well-made sentence — it is simply a 2002 sentence.

Adaptation drift is the mechanism. A viewer hears a line in a Dickens film, remembers it as Dickens, and posts it; the next person adds a book title to make it look sourced. Lydia Craig’s study of internet Dickens “quotes” in Dickens Quarterly names this exact route, and McGrath’s Nicholas Nickleby specifically, as a source of lines the novelist never wrote. The same screenplay gave the internet “Happiness is a gift and the trick is not to expect it, but to delight in it when it comes” — also Crummles, also filed on quote sites under Dickens.
context.detailsSummary: How “Mugby Junction” got attached to it
detailsBody: Most quote sites give the line no source at all. The ones that do usually say Mugby Junction — Dickens’s 1866 railway-station collection — which is puzzling until you look at why.

A print-on-demand publisher, A Word To The Wise, issued an edition of Mugby Junction in August 2013 whose listed title is literally Mugby Junction: “Family not only need to consist of merely those whom we share blood, but also for those whom we’d give blood.” The quote is cover copy, harvested from the web, not a line from the book. Retail listings then made it look like a citation, and the attribution loop closed on itself.

The Project Gutenberg text of Mugby Junction contains the word “blood” nine times — a nosebleed, a murder, a torrent of it rushing to a narrator’s face, “no blood-money” — and not once in anything resembling this sentiment.
context.pull: An adaptation puts words in a dead novelist’s mouth. The internet then signs his name.

sourcesVerified.claim: Goodreads carries "Family not only need to consist of merely those whom we share blood, but also for those whom we'd give blood" attributed to Charles Dickens with no book or source named, at 407 likes.

Goodreads carries the variant "Family need not be defined merely as those with whom we share blood, but as those for whom we would give our blood" attributed to Charles Dickens and sourced to Nicholas Nickleby.

Quotes.net attributes "They came to see that family need not be defined merely as those with whom they share blood but for those for whom they would give their blood" to Mr. Crummles in the 2002 film Nicholas Nickleby.

The Quotes.net page for Nicholas Nickleby (2002) transcribes Crummles's narration including "We must build a new family, person by person", the family/blood line, and "Happiness is a gift and the trick is not to expect it, but to delight in it when it comes".
Douglas McGrath wrote and directed Nicholas Nickleby (2002); US release 27 December 2002; Nathan Lane plays Vincent Crummles and also narrates the film.

Douglas McGrath was born 12 February 1958 in Midland, Texas and died 3 November 2022 in New York City aged 64; American screenwriter, director, playwright and actor; co-wrote Bullets Over Broadway (1994), wrote and directed Emma (1996) and directed Nicholas Nickleby (2002).

Wikiquote's Charles Dickens page does not contain the family/blood quote in any section; its only Misattributed entry is the "every one for himself, and Providence for us all" line credited to Charles Reade.

A print-on-demand edition titled 'Mugby Junction: "Family not only need to consist of merely those whom we share blood, but also for those whom we'd give blood."' was published by A Word To The Wise with a release date of 20 August 2013.

Loyola University Chicago reports Lydia Craig's finding that Dickens "never said or wrote many of these quotes" and that "Occasionally, they were derived from screenplays of Dickens films, such as Douglas McGrath's Nicholas Nickleby."
Lydia Craig, "What Charles Dickens Never Said: Verifying Internet 'Quotes' and Accessing the Works with Online Resources," Dickens Quarterly 37, no. 3 (2020): 249–263, DOI 10.1353/dqt.2020.0033.
Charles Dickens was born 7 February 1812 and died 9 June 1870; Nicholas Nickleby was serialised 1838–39.
Project Gutenberg hosts the full text of Charles Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby (serialised 1838–1839), public domain in the USA.
Project Gutenberg hosts the full text of Mugby Junction, a collection of short stories written in 1866 with Charles Dickens as primary author.

The plain-text Project Gutenberg edition of Nicholas Nickleby contains no instance of "share blood", "give blood", "give their blood" or "give our blood" (verified by downloading and grepping the file).

The plain-text Project Gutenberg edition of Mugby Junction contains no instance of "share blood", "give blood", "give their blood" or "give our blood"; its nine uses of "blood" are all unrelated (verified by downloading and grepping the file).
